meta.title: Quosparr: Codex, Claude Code and Grok quota in your menu bar
meta.description: Quosparr is a free, native menu bar and system tray app for macOS, Windows and Linux. Track Codex, Claude Code and Grok subscription quota, reset credits, API-equivalent cost and local sessions.

hero.tagline: A small sparrow perched in your menu bar, keeping watch over your Codex, Claude, and Grok quota.
hero.description: A native menu bar and system tray app for macOS, Windows and Linux. See subscription quota, reset credits, API-equivalent cost and local sessions at a glance, with separate accounts for each provider.

features.title: Features
features.lead: Codex, Claude Code and Grok each get their own tab. Quota, cost and accounts stay separate per provider.
codex: Remaining quota for the 5-hour, weekly and additional windows, with account, plan and expiry
Reset credit count, status and expiry time
Weekly allowance estimate compared with previous weeks, to spot quota cuts
Account switching, recent sessions and repair of the local session index
claude: Claude Code subscription usage for the 5-hour, 7-day and per-model weekly windows, plus extra usage
Token usage, API-equivalent cost, recent sessions and output speed from local session logs
Import and switch subscription accounts; MCP tokens are kept when you switch
grok: Included quota with a Build / Imagine / Chat breakdown, prepaid balance and on-demand usage
Multiple OAuth / SuperGrok accounts with isolated sign-in and explicit switching
Recent sessions from local Grok CLI logs

common.title: Menu bar at a glance
common.text: Follow the active tab, or keep up to two providers in the menu bar.

common.title: API-equivalent cost
common.text: Today, this cycle, last cycle, this month or a custom range, computed from local logs.

common.title: Token charts
common.text: Year-to-date usage as a heatmap, line or bar chart, by day, week or cumulative.

common.title: Themes and languages
common.text: Light, dark or system appearance, in seven languages.

common.title: Updates and widgets
common.text: Built-in signed updates on all three platforms, and desktop widgets on macOS 14+.

common.title: Network proxy
common.text: Follow the system, or use HTTP or SOCKS5. Proxy passwords stay in the system credential store.

shots.title: Screenshots
shots.note: The screenshots show v1 on macOS and Windows.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: Quosparr reads local CLI files and talks only to each provider's own endpoints, public status and price sources, and GitHub for updates. There is no Quosparr server.

items.title: Its own data folder
items.text: Derived, non-secret data lives in ~/.quosparr. No app cache is written into ~/.codex.

items.title: Credentials stay on your machine
items.text: Managed account copies are stored with owner-only permissions, and account indexes never contain tokens.

items.title: No tokens in logs
items.text: Tokens and API keys never appear in logs, self-check output or issue templates.

items.title: Cost is computed locally
items.text: API-equivalent cost comes from local session logs. Session content is never uploaded.

items.title: Careful writes
items.text: Official login files change only on token refresh or when you confirm a switch. Session repair backs up the index first.

download.title: Download
download.lead: Pick the package for your system and CPU. Every package bundles its SQLite runtime, so the first launch downloads nothing extra.
download.macReq: macOS 12 or later. Desktop widgets need macOS 14+.
download.macNote: The app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized. If macOS cannot verify the developer, right-click Quosparr.app and choose Open, or click Open Anyway in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
download.macFix: If macOS says the app is damaged, move it to Applications and run:
download.winNote: Installs for the current user into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Quosparr. No administrator rights needed.
download.linuxReq: Needs GTK3, AppIndicator, a desktop with a system tray, and a Secret Service session such as GNOME Keyring or KWallet.
download.linuxNote: Install the .deb with your package manager, or put install.sh next to the .tar.gz and run sh install.sh to install into ~/.local.
